To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a single neural network architecture can be used to jointly learn many natural language processing (NLP) tasks; 2) multitask learning improves the performance of the individual shared tasks; 3) semi-supervised learning improves the performance even more; and 4) the combination of multitask and semi-supervised approaches is the most effective.

1) a unified neural network architecture for natural language tasks can achieve state-of-the-art performance on a variety of tasks, 2) multitask learning improves the generalization of neural networks, 3) semi-supervised learning can improve the generalization performance of neural networks, and 4) the combination of multitask and semi-supervised approaches leads to further performance gains.

(i) a single neural network architecture trained jointly on a variety of tasks using weight-sharing can outperform the state-of-the-art on a number of tasks, (ii) a language model learnt on large unlabeled text improves performance on the shared tasks, (iii) the language model can be trained using the shared task predictions as a regularization mechanism.
